speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they appeared at the same time.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That 3-day history of worsening wrist pain with chills and malaise, following a self-resolving knee issue after camping in Minnesota, is very concerning for a septic joint. Given your recent sexual activity, are you currently experiencing any genital sores, discharge, or painful urination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your wrists and hands, combined with fever and severe tenderness after camping in Minnesota, is highly suggestive of a specific infection. Did you have any eye or mouth sores, and is there any history of tick bites? I need to see the lesions to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist and hand skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease (Bartonella henselae) presenting with paronychia and regional lymphadenopathy. The combination of violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands, a history of a self-resolving knee injury (likely a cat scratch), and camping in an endemic area is highly specific. While the sexual history suggests STI workup, the clinical picture strongly points to Bartonella.
